Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

I get up · she works · he goes
SubjectVerbExample
I / you / we / theyverbI get up at 7.
he / she / itverb + sShe gets up at 7.
spellinggo→goes, study→studiesHe goes to work.
with timeat / on / inShe starts work at 9 on Monday.
  • I / you / we / they → verb: I get up, they work.
  • he / she / it → verb + s: she works, he gets up.
  • Spelling: go → goes, watch → watches, study → studies.
  • With time: I start work at 9 on Monday in the morning.

→ Negative & questions (I don't / Do you…?) come next.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: I get up → she getS up. He/she/it adds -s: work → works, go → goes, watch → watches.
  • ⚠ One small -s carries 'he/she': she workS. Forgetting it is the number one error at this level.

Listening

Listen. Then choose True or False.

You can listen again.

🔊 Helena's day — Oxford Navigate audiolisten, then answer
1Helena gets up at 5.00.
2She goes to work by bus.
3She starts work at 8.00.
4Her husband works.
5She has nine children.
6All her children live at home.
7She goes to bed at ten.
8On Saturday evenings she watches a film.
Why these answers

Helena gets up at 5.00, goes to work by train, starts at 8.00. Her husband doesn't work; they have nine children (seven at home). She goes to bed at ten and watches a film on Saturday evenings.

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write two short lines about your daily routine: I get up at … / I go to bed at … .

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

I get up at seven. I have breakfast at eight and I go to work at nine. In the evening I watch TV. I go to bed at eleven.

Check yourself:

  • Did you use Present Simple verbs (I get up, I go)?
  • Did you add a time (at seven, in the evening)?
  • For he/she — did you add -s (he gets, she goes)?
